purpose: Real-data forecasting pool for the H1/H3 forecasting cell (cycle 3).

archive.name: Monash Time Series Forecasting Archive
archive.paper: Godahewa, Bergmeir, Webb, Hyndman, Montero-Manso (2021), Monash Time Series Forecasting Archive, NeurIPS Datasets and Benchmarks. arXiv:2105.06643

datasets.cite: Makridakis, Spiliotis, Assimakopoulos (2020), The M4 competition: 100,000 time series and 61 forecasting methods, International Journal of Forecasting
datasets.chronos_split_evidence: IN the Chronos training corpus. arXiv:2403.07815 Table 2 lists 'M4 (Hourly)' under in-domain evaluation with 414 series of length 748-1008, which matches this file exactly. CORRECTED 2026-11-14: this entry previously read UNVERIFIED.

datasets.cite: Ben Taieb, Bontempi, Atiya, Sorjamaa (2012), A review and comparison of strategies for multi-step ahead time series forecasting based on the NN5 forecasting competition, Expert Systems with Applications
datasets.chronos_split_evidence: NOT in the Chronos training corpus. Table 2 lists 'NN5 (Daily)' under zero-shot evaluation with 111 series of length 791, matching this file exactly. CORRECTED 2026-11-14: previously read UNVERIFIED.

datasets.cite: UCI Machine Learning Repository, ElectricityLoadDiagrams20112014, via the Monash archive
datasets.chronos_split_evidence: IN the Chronos training corpus. Table 2 lists 'Electricity (Hourly)' under in-domain evaluation with 321 series of length 26304, matching this file exactly. CORRECTED 2026-11-14: previously read LIKELY.

datasets.cite: California Department of Transportation PEMS, via the Monash archive
datasets.chronos_split_evidence: NOT in the Chronos training corpus. Table 2 lists 'Traffic' under zero-shot evaluation with 862 series of length 17544, matching this file exactly. CORRECTED 2026-11-14: this entry previously read DOCUMENTED OVERLAP, which was a guess made before the tables were read and is wrong.

datasets.cite: Godahewa et al. (2021), Monash Time Series Forecasting Archive; sourced from Australian weather stations
datasets.chronos_split_evidence: Table 2 lists 'Weather' under zero-shot evaluation with 3010 series of length 1332-65981, matching this file.
datasets.added: 2026-11-14 (cycle 3): the only source of weak-seasonality series long enough for the L=512 geometry.

datasets.cite: McCracken & Ng (2016), FRED-MD: A Monthly Database for Macroeconomic Research, Journal of Business & Economic Statistics; via the Monash archive
datasets.chronos_split_evidence: Table 2 lists 'FRED-MD' under zero-shot evaluation with 107 series of length 728, matching this file.
datasets.added: 2026-11-14 (cycle 3): monthly economic series, the non-sensor arm.

reproduce: python data-real/fetch.py           # re-download from Zenodo, verify sha256

pools.chronos_contamination: MIXED: 2 of 4 datasets (m4_hourly, electricity_hourly) are Benchmark I, i.e. in the Chronos training corpus.
pools.use: H1 only. A within-forecaster contrast across L is unharmed by contamination, which hits all five history lengths equally. NOT valid for a cross-arm headline.

pools.chronos_contamination: CONTROLLED for Chronos: every dataset is Benchmark II. NOT controlled for the bare LLM arm - these archives are public text.
pools.use: H3 and the cross-arm ride-along; any 'the tool beats the LLM' claim.

pools.chronos_contamination: CONTROLLED for Chronos: every dataset is Benchmark II.
pools.use: the reframed H2 (weak vs strong seasonality) at L=128. Two-sample, not paired: the strata are different series.

chronos_reference.paper: Ansari et al. (2024), Chronos: Learning the Language of Time Series, arXiv:2403.07815
chronos_reference.table: Table 2, Appendix B - partitions every dataset into pretraining-only / in-domain evaluation (Benchmark I, 15 datasets, used in training) / zero-shot evaluation (Benchmark II, 27 datasets, not used in training)
chronos_reference.verified: 2026-11-14, by matching series count and series length against each .tsf file
chronos_reference.caveat: This settles contamination for the HARNESS arm (Chronos) only. The bare LLM arm is not controlled: these archives are public text and Qwen2.5 may carry the literal values. Only data published after the backbone's training cutoff would settle that.
